content:
Truckers in Nuevo Laredo are standing down, at least for now, after Mexico's Interior Ministry (Segob) and national trucking organizations agreed Tuesday, Oct. 27, to end highway blockades and suspend protests in exchange for work tables to address the sector's demands, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The agreement, reached after a meeting with the Cámara Nacional del Autotransporte de Carga (Canacar), commits participating organizations to definitively remove blockades and suspend freight protests, Segob said. Four work tables were set up to take up highway security, infrastructure, tax issues, social security and labor conditions, with Segob's undersecretariat and Government Unit coordinating follow-up, according to national reports of the ministry's statement.

For Nuevo Laredo, the pause follows two days of local mobilization. Truckers joined a national mobilization Monday, Oct. 26, and on Tuesday about 50 trailers protested on the highway — stopping on the road, not on the international bridge — according to earlier local coverage. Leaders told drivers to disperse and return to their places of origin, leaving highways clear, according to national trucking leaders quoted in the coverage.

The suspension is temporary in the sense that the underlying demands are not yet resolved: the work tables are meant to produce concrete results, and the sector's complaints — including highway insecurity, attacks on drivers, extortion, over-regulation and deteriorating infrastructure — remain on the table, according to the trucking organizations. No new mobilizations were announced as part of the agreement.

For a border city whose economy runs on cross-border freight, the end of the blockades removes an immediate disruption to highway circulation, even as the negotiations that will decide whether the peace holds are just beginning.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Transportistas suspenden temporalmente las manifestaciones tras mesas de diálogo con Gobernación," Oct. 27, 2026
  • Secretaría de Gobernación (Segob) statement on the Canacar agreement, Oct. 27, 2026
  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Así fue la protesta de 50 tráileres en Nuevo Laredo," Oct. 27, 2026

Update — November 5, 2026

The work tables agreed to on October 27 have begun producing dates and meetings, though the core highway-security table still has no date. On November 3, the four trucking organizations — Canacar, HAMOTAC, FEMATRAC and INDECO — met with the Labor Ministry (STPS), which committed to publish the guidelines for electronic registration of drivers' workdays no later than November 15, 2026, according to Canacar and trade-press reports of the meeting. The ministry said implementation would be gradual and flexible, with possible adjustments for specially regulated activities such as trucking, and that driving, availability, waiting and rest time would be distinguished, with no single technology platform imposed. Truckers also met with Finance Minister Édgar Amador Zamora to press for fiscal measures recognizing the sector's operating reality, including the fiscal stimulus, the IEPS fuel tax, vehicle scrappage and administrative facilities, Canacar reported. No new blockade or protest has been announced, and the security work table remains unscheduled, according to T21.

Sources: T21 — "Transportistas expresan preocupación por registro electrónico de jornadas laborales" (Nov. 5, 2026); Megavisión — "Transportistas piden a Hacienda condiciones ajustadas a la realidad del sector" (Nov. 5, 2026); Factor Automotor — "Transportistas y STPS abordan reducción de la jornada laboral" (Nov. 4, 2026).

Update — November 8, 2026

The highway-security work table met Thursday, November 5, and produced the first concrete security commitments since the October 27 agreement. The National Guard told trucking representatives it will add 826 officers to highway patrols, drawn from the Military College and finishing training at the Police Academy in San Luis Potosí, with deployment in the coming days, though no exact date was given, according to T21, citing FEMATRAC national president Lauro Rincón Hernández. The organizations also pressed for a permanent Guard presence, patrols and a revised security strategy in the states with the most cargo theft. On Friday, November 6, Canacar, Hamotac, Fematrac, Indeco and the business confederation Concanaco-Servytur signed agreements with the federal Security Cabinet — the Public Security Ministry, the National Guard and the Attorney General's Office — in Segob-coordinated dialogue tables, committing to three lines of action against extortion and abuses of authority on highways: uniform criteria among state prosecutors to speed the release of vehicles held after criminal incidents, direct complaint channels with Segob and the Attorney General's Office, and state-level work tables plus evaluation of real-time risk-monitoring technology, according to La Verdad. The organizations said they expect to see progress before the end of 2026, and further follow-up tables with security authorities and the Attorney General's Office are planned, T21 reported. No new blockade or protest has been announced.

Sources: T21 — "Guardia Nacional alista más de 800 elementos para reforzar seguridad carretera" (Nov. 6, 2026); La Verdad — "Transportistas acuerdan con Segob frenar extorsión en carreteras" (Nov. 6, 2026).

excerpt: After two days of mobilization — including a 50-trailer protest on the highway Tuesday — Nuevo Laredo truckers are suspending protests under a Segob–Canacar deal that trades lifted blockades for four work tables on security, infrastructure, taxes and labor conditions.
title: Nuevo Laredo truckers suspend protests after Segob deal sets up four work tables
